newsitem.title: USA: Key senators see Albright approval.
newsitem.headline: Key senators see Albright approval.

text.p: Key senators Wednesday signaled confidence that Madeleine Albright would easily win committee endorsement and full Senate approval to be the first woman secretary of state.

Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms said after a day-long confirmation hearing the panel would vote on Albright's nomination on Jan.20 -- earlier if possible -- "and I don't have any doubt as to how it's coming out."

Sen Joseph Biden, the committee's ranking Democrat, said if the panel vote takes place as expected, Helms is considering waiving the so-called three day rule so the full Senate can approve Albright's appointment the very next day, on Jan 21, instead of waiting three days to act on the matter.

Biden publicly thanked Helms for going out of his way to expedite Albright's historic confirmation. The chairman "is going the extra yard. This is a bit unusual in the sense that he's being as he always is being extremely accommodating in trying to do the buisiness of the committee," Biden said.
